question.problem:
What are the pivot columns of the matrix $P,$ given by

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 2 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 9 & -3 \\ 0 & 3 & -6 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & -6 & -3\end{aligned}]?
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we need to convert $P$ to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 2 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 9 & -3 \\ 0 & 3 & -6 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & -6 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 2 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 9 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & -6 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{4} & :={R}_{4}+2{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 2 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 9 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $P$ has $4$ pivots. In particular, the pivot columns are the $2$nd, $3$rd, $5$th, and $6$th columns.
